rites.name: Osulalmaira
rites.text: Osulalmaira is a concept of the Courts of Teleontanum, the first principle that the Council of Trials used to weigh whether a world may open its door to another. It is remembered as a standing law rather than a figure, invoked when the builders of doors hold their councils.

rites.name: Ryilara
rites.text: Ryilara is a concept of Teleontanum, the will that shapes the Courts, where divine trials decide who may build the doors between worlds. In the Age of the first sovereign it is bound to the groves and the growing kingdoms, and its judgments are said to be weighed in the sap of the oldest trees.

rites.name: Valaurnor
rites.text: Valaurnor is a concept of the Seeding in Teleontanum, the quiet time when the makers plant the Weave and dormant powers sleep beneath the growing groves. It is remembered as the seed-bearing principle that anchors the first sovereign's kingdom to the living land.

rites.name: Fenasten
rites.text: Fenasten is the concept of the Pact sworn in the Sundering, when worlds broke and their shards were bound together by oath. It is understood as the will that holds the broken worlds to their word rather than as any single body or voice.

rites.name: Ilyameth
rites.text: Ilyameth is the concept of the grove-rooted Fall that split Teleontanum's worlds apart, binding the broken pieces into the Pact sworn at the first sovereign's accession. It is remembered in the groves and growing kingdoms as the principle by which sundered things are made to hold together again.

rites.name: Kelardonen
rites.text: Kelardonen is a concept of the Teleontanum, a principle of holding that the Walled Age's orders believed kept the flame of the world from spilling into the cold. Its adherents built temples around the idea that a sworn wall could bind even the mightiest current of the Holy Age.

rites.name: Thazis
rites.text: Thazis is a concept of the Walled Age in Teleontanum, a principle that a wall holds only as long as those who keep it remember why it was raised. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between holding orders, its adherents taught that a sundered bond could be remade by a single deliberate crossing. Its power was felt most in the first crossings, when a people chose to step beyond their walls.

rites.name: Voraggak
rites.text: Voraggak is a concept in the Teleontanum cosmos, a hungry branch-eater that feeds on unrealized endings during the Three Futures, when the Library shelves every outcome. It is less a creature than a pressure that thins the shelves whenever a possibility is quietly left unchosen.

rites.name: Osulanala
rites.text: Osulanala is the concept of a branching ending, the moment in Teleontanum when the Three Futures diverge and the Library shelves each outcome as a separate sealed volume. It is not a being but a principle that the Library itself consults when no single future can be chosen by the living.
